> type: ", ch

> chipType)
> at getSnpInformation.AffymetrixCdfFile(cdf)
> at getSnpInformation(cdf)

Which CDF do you use for your GWS5 analysis? The UFL files provided
are for the "full" (and "alternative") CDF called
GenomeWideSNP_5.Full.r2.cdf. It does not match the units in the
"default" CDF, e.g. GenomeWideSNP_5.cdf or the "default/alternative"
GenomeWideSNP_5.r2.cdf.

My best guess from your output is that you are using the "default" CDF
named GenomeWideSNP_5.cdf (or possibly GenomeWideSNP_5.r2.cdf), and in
such cases aroma.affymetrix cannot find a corresponding UFL file
(you'll have the same problem later with the UGP file).

Are you aware of vignette "Total Copy Number Analysis (5.0 & 6.0)"? See

http://groups.google.com/group/aroma-affymetrix/web/total-copy-number-analysis-6-0

Make sure to follow to follow the instructions under "Annotation data"
carefully. Especially the part saying that you need to rename
"GenomeWideSNP_5.Full.r2.cdf" to "GenomeWideSNP_5,Full,r2.cdf" (note
commas). I know this is a little bit annoying having to rename files
like this. I am trying to come up with a safe way for
aroma.affymetrix to recognize both version, but until then you have to
rename the files.

>
>
> One possible work around is to rename the ufl and ugp files- so that
> they appear as dChip files (snp_info, etc).
> When I do so, the files are read in - is there any danger in this
> fix?

>
> 20071218 19:42:08|Defining DChipSnpInformation from chip type...

> 20071218 19:42:08| Located pathname: annotationData/chipTypes/
> GenomeWideSNP_5/dChip/SNP5_snp_info.txt
> 20071218 19:42:08| Instantiating DChipSnpInformation...
> DChipSnpInformation:
> Name: SNP5_snp_info
> Tags:
> Pathname: annotationData/chipTypes/GenomeWideSNP_5/dChip/
> SNP5_snp_info.txt
> File size: 3.51MB
> RAM: 0.00MB
> Chip type: GenomeWideSNP_5
> 20071218 19:42:09| Instantiating DChipSnpInformation...done
> 20071218 19:42:09|Defining DChipSnpInformation from chip type...done
>
> >print(si)
>
> ##returns
> DChipSnpInformation:
> Name: SNP5_snp_info
> Tags:
> Pathname: annotationData/chipTypes/GenomeWideSNP_5/dChip/
> SNP5_snp_info.txt
> File size: 3.51MB
> RAM: 0.00MB
> Chip type: GenomeWideSNP_5

No, that will not work. Now aroma.affymetrix thinks the file is of
the dChip file format. I am actually surprised that aroma.affymetrix
does not throw an exception - at least it should when later try to use
it.

Basically, you should *never* ever have to do hacks such a renaming
annotation files to get things working, that is, unless I explicitly
have written so somewhere (as in the above case, but that's rare). In
other words, it is better to ask for help when you're in doubt, as you
did.

If you follow the above vignette, it should work smoothly. In that
vignette the validity of the UFL and UGP files are tested before you
start your analysis. Let me know if it helps.

For future correspondence, please provide your sessionInfo() output.

Cheers

Henrik

>
> Thanks,
> Christina
>

Taking the chance for the same announcement again: If you find
yourself having to do ad hoc hacks to get things working, then it most
likely means you're heading in the wrong direction. Please unlearn
any such trick that you might have picked up elsewhere. My way of
design and implement tools is so you don't have to do that.

Yes, most likely the problem was not using the latest version of the package;

Version: 0.8.2 [2007-12-10]
o In general, there is now better support for tagged CDFs. For
instance, AffymetrixCdfFile$fromName("HuEx-1_0-st-v2", tags="core")
can be used to locate 'HuEx-1_0-st-v2,core.CDF'.

> So, to ensure that I have the correct annotation files, I have gone
> back and repeated the steps outlined in "Building UFL file...".

Wow, so you're ahead of me. Ok, I've just uploaded the modified UFL
and updated the links and document. So, use the annotation files
specified and available for download, i.e.

GenomeWideSNP_5,Full,r2,na24,+.ugp
GenomeWideSNP_5,Full,r2,na24,HB20071209.ufl

together with GenomeWideSNP_5,Full,r2.cdf.

That should do for you analysis.

I guess you already read the details, but the NetAffx annotation data
files provided by Affymetrix for the GWS5 chip type are incorrect for
fragment length information. The previous
GenomeWideSNP_5,Full,r2,na24,+.ufl file had some of those problem.
I've made them aware of the problem and I hope they are working on a
fix before next NetAffx. The price we pay now is that we don't have
fragment-length annotation data for 6,323 SNPs. In the current
implementation of our fragment-length normalization method such SNPs
will unfortunately *not* be normalize but still be passed on. All
other calibration/normalization methods are unaffected.

I just give comment below, because you're not supposed to build your own UFLs.
